Trail Physics · Unit 2: Understanding Motion · Module 4

Motion in One Dimension

Position, displacement, velocity and acceleration, and the graphs and equations that describe a rider on a straight trail.

Lesson coming

The question

How far do you travel while you brake to a stop at the bottom of a descent?

The physics

  • Position and displacement
  • Speed and velocity
  • Acceleration and deceleration
  • Free fall
  • Motion graphs
  • Average vs. instantaneous velocity

The math

  • v = Δx / Δt
  • a = Δv / Δt
  • x = x₀ + v₀t + ½at²

Learning objectives

  • Tell distance from displacement, and speed from velocity
  • Calculate average velocity from a change in position
  • Calculate acceleration, including braking
  • Use the constant-acceleration equations to predict position and speed
  • Read and sketch position-, velocity- and acceleration-time graphs
  • Describe free fall, with g ≈ 9.8 m/s²

Helps to know first: Mathematics Review.

The mountain biking connection

Follow a rider along a straight trail: steady speed, speeding up, braking, stopping. Each one is a different shape on a position-time or velocity-time graph.
